content.text: Purpose

Turn a pattern of the learning loop (ADR-0053, 3.7) into a case and prepare open cases for the human — the server counts the patterns (threshold n = 3), the Builder phrases, assigns, and never decides.

Conventions: Load only the sections of the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource this playbook needs — before the first write step, in one call: fetch_resource(resource_id, block_ids=["res-conv-h-status", "res-conv-h-managed"]). A heading anchor returns its whole section; the resource_id is in this playbook's links (linked_blocks). Load other sections only when needed (anchors via list_resource_blocks).
Signpost — load only the path you take (d7-h-weg-a | d7-h-weg-b | d7-h-weg-c)

A run takes exactly one path (see Entry points). Fetch the playbook with format="outline", then the frame plus your path: fetch_playbook(playbook_id, block_ids=["d7-h-zweck", "d7-h-einstiege", "d7-h-grenzen", "d7-h-datenschutz", "d7-h-wegweiser", "<path>", "d7-h-vorlagen", "d7-h-werkzeuge", "d7-h-anti"]). Path B also needs d7-h-a5 (test case). If the run switches paths, load the new path.
Entry points — the two copy blocks
The patterns page in the feedback hub (tab Patterns) hands out a copy block per pattern. It contains only IDs, never content. Two wordings trigger this playbook:
Learning-suggestion pattern: “Turn learning suggestion {id} from {agent} into a case with situation, behaviour and expectation.” — continue with path A.

Case pattern: “Summarise the open cases {ids} for {agent} and propose a change to {element}.” — continue with path B. “Open” here means every case not yet closed: open, triaged, in_progress and reopened (see B1).
Without a copy block (“prepare the open cases”, “assign the cases”, “show me the patterns”) — read patterns with list_patterns or continue with path C.

{agent} is the agent's name. list_agents returns its UUID; if several agents share the name, ask, don't guess. list_patterns(agent_id) returns the current patterns with threshold, time window and evidence_ids (evidence); use them to cross-check the IDs of a copy block.
Role and boundaries — party, not judge

Allowed via MCP (case_triage): read patterns (list_patterns), read cases (list_cases, get_case), read learning suggestions verbatim (get_lesson, only kind=lesson), assign elements (assign_case_elements, including model_limit), set cases to triaged (triage_case), convert a learning suggestion into a case (convert_lesson_to_case, after approval), create test cases (create_test_case) and read them (list_test_cases), create drafts on elements (update_* creates a draft).

Never: set a case to addressed, dismissed or verified, delete a case, activate a version, reject a learning suggestion. Agent tokens cannot do this server-side (ADR-0053, 3.3, F-W7) — don't try. The server sets in_progress when a submitted record contains a measure for the case (switch W-E2 a); there is no separate call for it.
Human-only in the web UI: dismiss or delete a case, reject a learning suggestion, activate a version, rate a follow-up.
No detours: no REST calls bypassing MCP, no raw data from other sources. If a tool is missing, say “the human does that in the web UI” and supply the text for it.
Data protection — don't carry case content forward
Cases and learning suggestions can contain personal data (names, addresses, customer data, quotes from conversations). Therefore:
Never copy case content verbatim into playbook, resource, persona or test case texts. Those carry the abstracted rule, not the individual case.
Phrase test case inputs synthetically: same situation, invented neutral data (e.g. “Customer A”, “Project X”).
Limit the case texts you phrase to the behavior. If the source contains personal data, replace it with roles (“the user”, “a customer”) and tell the human.
In hand-offs and Kanban comments name only IDs and shortened, neutral summaries.
Path A — Learning-suggestion pattern: phrase the case and convert
A1 — Read the learning suggestion

get_lesson(memory_id) returns the wording of the learning suggestion, even if it belongs to another agent of the workspace. The tool reads only entries with kind=lesson; anything else answers with memory_not_found. Check the status: only an open (pending) learning suggestion can be converted. Without the wording you phrase nothing — no case can be derived from the ID alone.

Optionally as context: list_cases(agent_id, status=[open, triaged, in_progress, reopened]) shows whether cases on the same topic already exist. If there is an open case with the same expectation, say so: then the learning suggestion is more likely evidence for that case than a new one.
A2 — Phrase situation, behavior, expected
Situation (situation): when does it occur? Trigger and context, without personal data.
Behavior (behavior): what did the agent do? Observable, without judgement.
Expected (expected_behavior): what would have been right? Phrase it as a checkable rule — it later becomes the expectation of a test case.
Optionally impact (impact) and a proposal for the severity (low, medium, high), always marked as a proposal.
Phrase only what the wording supports. The counter says that something recurs, not why. Cause hypotheses belong, marked as such, in a separate line “Hypothesis” and not in the case text.
A3 — Convert after approval

First show the case text and get approval. Then convert_lesson_to_case(agent_id, memory_id, situation, behavior, expected_behavior, impact, severity, signal, source_ref). agent_id is the agent that owns the learning suggestion. The new case carries reporter_kind pattern and source_memory_id, the learning suggestion moves to converted, and the pattern disappears by itself.

A learning suggestion can be converted only once (memory_not_convertible). If this error comes back, check with list_cases whether the case already exists instead of creating a second one. If the human rejects the case, the learning suggestion stays pending; only the human can reject it in the memory.
A4 — report_case is not the path for learning suggestions

report_case creates a case with reporter_kind builder, without a link to the learning suggestion. The learning suggestion would stay pending and the pattern visible, and a second case for the same pattern looms. For learning-suggestion patterns therefore always use convert_lesson_to_case. Use report_case only for an own observation without a learning suggestion and only on explicit request.
A5 — Create a test case

Propose a test case for the new case: title, input (synthetic), expected behavior (= expected), check kind (human_rule, or must_contain / must_not_contain with check_pattern if the rule can be checked against a word) and the affected element (entity_type and entity_id, only together). After approval create_test_case(origin_case_id, agent_id, …). The test case is a prerequisite for every later measure (3.6).
Path B — Case pattern: summarize and propose a change
For case patterns you don't create a new case — not even a collective case. The cases already exist. Your contribution is the summary and a change proposal for the element.
B1 — Read the cases

“Open” in the copy block means not only status open but every case not yet closed: open, triaged, in_progress and reopened (ADR-0053, 3.7). A case pattern groups cases with the same element assignment — so these cases are assigned and usually already on triaged. Whoever reads only status=open misses exactly them.

Therefore: list_cases(agent_id, status=[open, triaged, in_progress, reopened], format=full) in one call. If the response returns next_cursor, page on with cursor until all IDs from the copy block are found. If an ID is still missing afterwards, say so explicitly instead of skipping it. get_case(case_id) returns a case's assignments, accounts and history.
B2 — Read the element and test cases

Read the element in its current state: fetch_playbook, fetch_resource, get_persona, get_system_prompt or get_agent (for tool_policy). In addition list_test_cases(agent_id, entity_type, entity_id) — which test cases exist already? — and get_feedback for element signals. Check whether is_managed is set.
B3 — Summarize

The common core of the cases in two to four sentences: situation, recurring behavior, shared expectation. Then the differences between the cases. No quotes with personal data, no reinterpretation of the count. If the expectations contradict each other, that is a finding for the human, not a decision for you.
B4 — Change proposal
The smallest change to the element, with location (section or block_id) and wording before/after.
Success criterion: how the follow-up shows that it works (e.g. the test case passes, no new cases on the element).
Counterposition: what speaks against the change, including the reach — how many agents use the element (find_usages).
At least one alternative with a trade-off, e.g. playbook step versus resource paragraph, or model_limit instead of a change.
A test case as in A5 (d7-h-a5); if one is missing, create it after approval with create_test_case from one of the cases.
B5 — Continue in the feedback conversation

If the human wants the change, it becomes a measure: that runs through the playbook “Moderate Feedback Conversation (Review)” (record with submit_session_protocol, then draft and link_measure_draft). Only this way do the cases move to in_progress and the follow-up measures the effect. Writing a draft without a record is possible but loses the link to the cases — tell the human.
Managed element (is_managed): no write, but a repo hand-off plus submit_feedback on the element.
tool_policy: update_agent takes effect immediately and is not versioned. Only with explicit approval of exactly this policy change, otherwise leave it as a proposal.
model_limit: no change. That is a result, not an assignment.
Path C — Prepare open cases for the human
C1 — Read

list_cases(status=[open, reopened], format=full), restricted to one agent if needed (agent_id); page on with next_cursor. Here only open and reopened are meant on purpose: cases waiting for an assignment or a reassessment. Cases on triaged are already assigned; they belong to path B or into a feedback conversation. Note per case the situation, behavior, expected, severity and reporter.
C2 — Determine the element

get_agent shows persona, template and tool_policy of the affected agent; get_persona its playbooks; fetch_playbook or fetch_resource the passages that steer the behavior. get_case shows an account of the agent if it gave one. Assign to the element whose instruction carried the behavior or should have carried it. Targets: persona, playbook, resource, external_tool, system_prompt_template, memory (with entity_id) as well as tool_policy and model_limit (without entity_id).
model_limit if the instruction was clear and present and the model still does not follow it — “model limit, no change makes sense”. That is an assessment the human confirms.
C3 — Assign

First output the assignment proposals with reasoning as a list, then get approval (individually or as a batch), then assign_case_elements. Mind the replace semantics: the call replaces the entire previous assignment. Read the current state beforehand with get_case (elements) and always pass the complete target list. The call's response is the new assignment — proofread it.
C4 — Classify (triaged)

After the assignment and with approval triage_case(case_id, note). The tool sets only triaged, only from open or reopened and only with at least one assignment (otherwise case_transition_forbidden). The note is optional and describes the assignment, not a verdict. If you consider a case dismissable (duplicate, no misbehavior), write that as a recommendation with reasoning in the report — only the human can dismiss.
Output templates

Path A — Case: agent {name} ({uuid}), learning suggestion {id}. Situation: … Behavior: … Expected: … Impact (optional): … Severity (proposal): … Test case proposal: title, input, expectation, check kind. Approval: convert yes/no, create test case yes/no. After writing: case ID, test case ID.

Path B — Summary: cases {ids} for {agent}, element {element}. Found: per ID with status (open/triaged/in_progress/reopened) or “missing”. Core: … Differences: … Change proposal: location, before, after. Success criterion: … Counterposition: … Alternative: … Test case: present (ID) or proposal. Next step: feedback conversation yes/no.

Path C — Triage preparation per case: case ID, short situation (neutral), proposed assignment, reasoning in one sentence, recommendation (classify / model limit / check dismissal). Then: approval for assignments and classification (triage_case).
Pitfalls

All case tools except report_case require case_triage. list_cases takes status as a list and pages via cursor/next_cursor. report_case only for your own observation and on request — not for learning suggestions (see A4). update_* and transition_* only up to review, writing only after approval.
Anti-patterns
Creating a new collective case from a case pattern.
Using report_case instead of convert_lesson_to_case for learning-suggestion patterns — that leaves the learning suggestion pending and the pattern standing.
Copying case content verbatim into test cases or playbooks.
Interpreting the count (“because the model can't do X”) without the wording supporting it.
Calling assign_case_elements without approval, without a prior get_case or with only the delta.
Setting a status the Builder is not entitled to, or trying to, or working around tool gaps via REST.
Reading only status=open for a case pattern and reporting assigned (triaged, in_progress) cases as “missing”.
Calling convert_lesson_to_case or triage_case without approval.
Notes

Basis: ADR-0053 sections 3.3 (case, status, permissions), 3.6 (measure, test case mandatory), 3.7 (patterns, reporter_kind pattern), 3.8 (case_triage), 6.5 to 6.7 (MCP tools); phase E tools per W-E1 b and PM-2/PM-4; delta spec phase D, S5 (copy blocks).
